true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition replaces the width/height method

Ruby does not overload methods. The new downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) at this line replaces the downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) defined just above, so that width/height version never runs. Existing callers that pass numeric max width and height (the previous public signature, which this file still tries to keep) will bind the width to dimensions and the height to opts. optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] and raises NoMethodError, or, if a hash is passed in the height slot, builds a geometry of just the width (for example "1024") instead of "1024x768". Thumbnail generation that still uses the old arity breaks. self.optimize's signature changed the same way (dimensions string instead of width, height), so any external optimize caller is broken too.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client upload limit is hardcoded and ignores per-type site settings

validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments had independent admin limits. It now always rejects above 10 * 1024 KB and no longer uses type. Attachments larger than max_attachment_size_kb but under 10MB are sent and then fail (or are stored, if the server trusts the client). Images the admin allowed above 10MB are blocked in the composer even though they would not need downsizing. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcode, so a proxy rejection is reported as a 10MB limit even when nginx or max_image_size_kb is different. uploads_controller.rb also downloads API URLs with a fixed 10.megabytes cap, so raising max_image_size_kb above 10MB cannot be honored on that path either.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
In-place downsize can corrupt the upload and the result is ignored

The new loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize with the same path for input and output (tempfile.path to tempfile.path) and ignores the boolean it returns. ImageMagick convert cannot safely read and write one file: it often truncates the destination before the source is fully read, so a failed or partial convert destroys the upload. The open Tempfile still refers to the original inode, so after convert replaces the path, tempfile.size and whatever Upload.create_for reads from the handle can stay on the old bytes or sit past the new EOF. The loop then either keeps shrinking a stale size or stores a corrupt/empty/original image. If convert or ImageOptim fails, execution still falls through to Upload.create_for. Five 80% passes also only reach about a third of the linear dimensions, so a file can remain over SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and still be uploaded.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

false_positives.candidate:
Oversized GIFs lose animation and SVGs are sent through convert

Auto-downsize always goes through OptimizedImage.downsize, whose non-animated instructions run convert with [0] (first frame only). The animated/gifsicle path is selected only when the filesystem path matches /\.GIF$/i. Rack and FileHelper temp paths do not keep the original filename extension, and this call never copies the bytes to a path ending in .gif, so allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails never takes effect. Every oversized GIF is flattened to one frame and that result is what gets stored as the original upload, even when animated thumbnails are allowed. The same branch also runs for any FileHelper.is_image? filename, including SVG, unlike OptimizedImage.create_for which copies SVGs instead of converting them. convert will fail or rasterize the SVG and that output is then saved under the original .svg name.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Nil host crashes before validation

before_validation calls self.host.sub! without checking host. Create/update with a missing or null embeddable_host[host] (the controller assigns params directly) raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error, so the admin API returns 500 rather than 422. Guard nil/blank host and let validates_format_of fail the save.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Update and destroy 500 when the host id is missing

update loads EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and passes it to save_host, which immediately writes host.host. destroy calls host.destroy on the same lookup. A stale or unknown id yields nil, so both actions raise NoMethodError instead of a 404. save_host also assumes params[:embeddable_host] is present; a body without that key raises before any error JSON is rendered.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Allow-list lookup drops ports and mishandles case

record_for_host sets host = uri.host and queries lower(host) = ? with that value unchanged. uri.host never includes the port, but the format validator and before_validation keep an optional :port on the stored host, so an entry saved as example.com:8080 never matches a referer of http://example.com:8080/... and host_allowed? stays false. The lower() call is also only applied to the column: a referer whose host has any capital letter (URI preserves case, so Example.com) compares lower(stored) = 'Example.com', which is never true, so the allow-list rejects it. Downcase the lookup value and compare host and port the same way they are stored.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are inserted raw and unquoted

Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted with execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)", bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation normalizer. The previous allow-list accepted http:// and https:// prefixes and paths (the old matcher used URI#host), but record_for_host compares only URI#host to the stored string. After upgrade, a saved value such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 will not match a referer host of discourse.org or example.com, so previously working embeds start returning invalid referer. A host containing a single quote also breaks the SQL or injects statements. Normalize (strip scheme, path, whitespace, and downcase) and insert with bound parameters. Windows newlines left by split("\n") have the same mismatch.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Category and embeddable-host fabricators are swapped

category_fabricator.rb now only defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), and the category, diff_category, happy_category, and private_category fabricators were moved into spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Specs still pass only because every fabricator file is auto-loaded. Anything that loads category_fabricator.rb by path, or a cleanup that deletes the category definitions from the embeddable-host file, will break Fabricate(:category) and Fabricate(:private_category) across the suite. Put each fabricator back in the file that matches its name.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are inserted raw and unquoted

Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted with execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)", bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation normalizer. The previous allow-list accepted http:// and https:// prefixes and paths (the old matcher used URI#host), but record_for_host compares only URI#host to the stored string. After upgrade, a saved value such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 will not match a referer host of discourse.org or example.com, so previously working embeds start returning invalid referer. A host containing a single quote also breaks the SQL or injects statements. Normalize (strip scheme, path, whitespace, and downcase) and insert with bound parameters. Windows newlines left by split("\n") have the same mismatch.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when embed_category is unset or unmatched

The data migration reads the old embed_category setting with execute(...)[0]['id'] and, only if that id is 0, does the same for uncategorized_category_id. Site settings at their default are often not stored, and embed_category was a free-text category name, so the join on categories.name commonly returns no row. [0] is then nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError before the category_id == 0 fallback. The same crash happens on the uncategorized lookup if that row is missing. Because this runs in the up migration that also deletes those settings, a typical upgrade aborts and never creates embeddable_hosts, while the new code no longer reads SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts. Handle an empty result and fall back to a real category id before inserting rows.

false_positives.candidate:
Any category_id is stored with no existence check

save_host assigns category_id from params and only substitutes uncategorized when the value is blank. There is no Category.exists? check, no model validation, and the migration adds no foreign key. A nonexistent id is saved. TopicEmbed.import then passes that id into PostCreator, so new embedded topics are created with a dangling category_id. Deleting a category later leaves the same dangling pointer because nothing cascades.

Host regex rejects hosts the old setting allowed

validates_format_of requires a dotted name ending in a letter TLD of 2 to 5 characters. The removed embeddable_hosts setting was a free-form host list. This regex rejects IPv4/IPv6, localhost, and any gTLD longer than 5 letters (.museum, .coffee, .international, and similar). Admins cannot save those hosts, and re-saving a migrated row fails validation, so those sites can no longer be allow-listed even though embedding used to work.

Hosts are not unique, so category lookup is arbitrary

Nothing validates uniqueness of host, and the new table has no unique index (case-insensitive or otherwise). The admin API and the migration can store duplicate hosts, including Example.com and example.com. record_for_host uses an unordered .first, so two rows for the same host with different categories make the imported topic category nondeterministic. Add a case-insensitive unique index and a matching validation.

New host API and migration have no behavioral tests

Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController specs only assert the class inherits AdminController. Nothing exercises create, update, destroy, a missing id, a blank category_id, or an invalid host, and there is no migration spec for missing embed_category / protocol-prefixed hosts. Those are the paths that 500 or drop existing allow-list entries, so the current suite will stay green if they are broken.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row

TopicsController#unsubscribe loads the per-user row with TopicUser.find_by and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If that row does not exist (logged-in user who can see the topic but has never had a topic_users record, or a category/mailing-list recipient whose row was never created), tu is nil and this raises NoMethodError. The email link then returns 500 and the notification level is not changed, so the unsubscribe action fails for exactly the people who need it. Use TopicUser.change (which inserts a row when missing) or create a muted row before updating.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Direct TopicUser save leaves notifications_reason_id nil so auto-track undoes the change

The new action assigns notification_level and calls save! instead of TopicUser.change. change is what sets notifications_changed_at, notifications_reason_id (user_changed), and the MessageBus notification_level_change event. Leaving notifications_reason_id nil means the existing auto-track logic in TopicUser.update_last_read and TopicUser.auto_track will treat the row as never explicitly chosen and set it back to tracking once the user has viewed the topic long enough (or on the next auto_track call). A successful mute is therefore silently reverted the next time they read the topic, and other open tabs are not told the level changed.

No coverage for the unsubscribe action or the new email link

The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into an existing MessageBuilder example so I18n interpolation does not raise, and still only asserts that the preferences URL is in the body. Nothing asserts the new per-topic sentence or URL, and there is no request/controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe. The nil TopicUser crash, the watching-to-regular branch, the missing notifications_reason_id, the slug redirect, and the wrong-session GET mutation would all merge unnoticed.

One-click unsubscribe does not stop notifications for watching or tracking users

The email copy and the new client string both say the link stops notifications for this topic, but the action only mutes when notification_level is regular or already muted. Watching (3) and tracking (2) are greater than regular, so they are downgraded to regular instead of muted. Regular still generates reply, mention, and quote notifications, so a user who is emailed because they are watching the topic — the main case for a per-topic unsubscribe link — keeps receiving those emails after one click. The confirmation page always claims notifications have stopped, and nothing tells them they must click again to actually mute.

Unsubscribe is a cookie-authenticated GET with no recipient token GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe (and /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe, which 301s to the slugged URL) changes notification state with no CSRF token and no per-recipient unsubscribe key. ensure_logged_in only checks the browser session. Any site can trigger it while the victim is logged in (for example an to /t//unsubscribe); the browser sends session cookies, follows the 301, and the second request mutates state. The link also is not bound to the user who was emailed: whoever is logged in is the account that is changed, so a shared browser, staff session, or forwarded mail unsubscribes the wrong person while the recipient keeps getting mail. Email link scanners that do send cookies can apply the change without a click, and because the handler is not idempotent for watching users a second fetch drops them from regular to muted. This needs a POST (or a one-time key like the digest unsubscribe key) that identifies the recipient.

Unsubscribe template will not be resolved by the new route

The route is registered as a top-level topicUnsubscribe at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe (app-route-map.js.es6). Ember resolves that to the template, controller, and view names topic-unsubscribe. The controller and view were added under those names, but the template was added at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which compiles to topic/unsubscribe and is only used by a nested topic.unsubscribe route. Nothing calls renderTemplate to bridge the gap, so after the server has already changed the notification level the confirmation UI throws a missing-template error (or renders an empty outlet). The stop-notifications copy and the notification-level dropdown never appear. Move the template to templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, or nest the route as topic.unsubscribe and move the controller/view to match.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Block-hit stats are rolled back on the signup they record

BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and last_match_at and calls record.save while it is invoked from EmailValidator during User validation. User#save runs validations inside the same database transaction, and a blocked address fails validation, so that transaction rolls back and undoes the BlockedEmail update. On a normal install (SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub? false) UsersController#create only calls save, so blocked signup attempts never persist match statistics — last_match_at stays nil and match_count stays 0, which is the signal the model spec says admins use to see whether a rule has ever matched. When call_discourse_hub? is true, create calls user.valid? (line 168) before save, so the first increment commits and the second is rolled back, and the counter moves by 1 instead of 2. The write has to happen outside the user transaction (separate connection, or after the user save/rollback), or the stats feature does not work for the block action.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Exact email match lets blocked addresses sign up

should_block? loads BlockedEmail with a case-sensitive where(email: email) and never strips or downcases. Signup stores whatever was posted (User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] raw), while change_email in UsersController canonicalizes with Email.downcase(...).strip. A row for user@evil.com therefore does not match User@evil.com, user@evil.com with surrounding whitespace, or other case variants, so the new block is bypassed by changing case or padding the address. Uniqueness on blocked_emails.email is also case-sensitive, so both casings can be stored and .first can return either row. Normalize on write (set_defaults) and on lookup the same way change_email does, and compare the normalized value, or the blocklist does not actually block.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Block-hit stats are rolled back on the signup they record

BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and last_match_at and calls record.save while it is invoked from EmailValidator during User validation. User#save runs validations inside the same database transaction, and a blocked address fails validation, so that transaction rolls back and undoes the BlockedEmail update. On a normal install (SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub? false) UsersController#create only calls save, so blocked signup attempts never persist match statistics — last_match_at stays nil and match_count stays 0, which is the signal the model spec says admins use to see whether a rule has ever matched. When call_discourse_hub? is true, create calls user.valid? (line 168) before save, so the first increment commits and the second is rolled back, and the counter moves by 1 instead of 2. The write has to happen outside the user transaction (separate connection, or after the user save/rollback), or the stats feature does not work for the block action.

Tests stub the block check and miss signup behavior

EmailValidator examples stub BlockedEmail.should_block?, so they never hit the database, never assert the user.email.blocked message, and never run User#save. BlockedEmail specs only call should_block? directly, which commits the counter outside a user transaction, so they stay green while a real blocked signup rolls the stats back and while a case or whitespace variant is allowed through. There is also no coverage that the domain whitelist/blacklist logic moved out of User still rejects addresses. A User create/save example with a real BlockedEmail row (including a different-case address) is needed or these failures ship untested.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
import_remote uses Kernel#open on attacker-influenced URLs

import_remote calls `open(url).read` without `require 'open-uri'` (unlike PollFeed) and without an http(s)-only client, timeout, or redirect check. If open-uri has not been loaded, Kernel#open treats the URL as a local filename and the fetch fails (Disqus import and embed retrieval blow up). Once open-uri is loaded, it follows redirects to any host with no read timeout, and non-URI strings fall through to file open or pipe execution. Embed URLs are supplied by visitors (TopicRetriever only compares URI#host to embeddable_host, not the scheme, and does not re-check redirects), and PollFeed does the same `open` on feed_polling_url. That is SSRF against internal HTTP services, worker hangs, and, for a non-http setting or feed link, local file read.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check is a substring match

The resize listener accepts a message when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1`. That is the wrong direction and is not an origin equality check. Any origin that is a prefix/substring of the configured forum URL passes, for example origin `http://forum.example.co` against discourseUrl `http://forum.example.com`, or any shorter prefix. A page that can postMessage to the host page (opener or another frame) can then set the embed iframe height. Compare the message origin to the parsed origin of discourseUrl (scheme, host, and port) instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Imported HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized

TopicEmbed.import appends the source URL into the post body with raw string interpolation (`<a href='#{url}'>`) and saves the whole document via PostCreator with cook_method raw_html and skip_validations. Post#cook then returns raw unchanged whenever cook_method is raw_html, so the normal PrettyText/Sanitize pipeline never runs. Cooked HTML is rendered with `raw` in the embed view and on the topic page. RSS items (PollFeed also runs CGI.unescapeHTML on the body, turning escaped markup back into tags) and any page fetched for an embed can therefore plant script, event handlers, or a quote-breaking URL such as http://host/?q='><script>… and get stored XSS in the forum origin. The existing sanitize gem is not used, and the topic embed spec locks in cooked == raw.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embed template has invalid ERB (`end if`)

The header conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which is not valid Ruby inside ERB. Rendering the success path (a topic id was found and best.html.erb is rendered) raises a SyntaxError/Template::Error, so the embed iframe 500s whenever a discussion already exists. It must be `<% end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed poll crashes on typical RSS items

poll_feed always does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then TopicEmbed.import. SimpleRSS leaves `content` nil for ordinary RSS 2.0 items that only have `description`/`summary`, so the first such item raises NoMethodError and the hourly job stops, importing nothing after it. String#scrub also does not exist on Ruby 2.0/1.9, which this app still references. There is no per-item rescue, and title/link can be missing the same way. Use a fallback (`content` or `description` or empty string), guard nil, and isolate item failures.

false_negatives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Cache miss runs a full feed import and drops HTTP fallback

When feed polling is enabled, perform_retrieve synchronously runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (download and import every feed item) inside the per-URL retrieve job, then only calls fetch_http if that returns normally and the URL is still missing. Any exception from the feed (network error, nil content, bad item) aborts the job before the single-page HTTP fetch, so the embed stays on the loading page forever. A single comment embed also triggers a full import with no timeout isolation.

Disqus import now depends on a live remote fetch and drops category

The importer used to create a local topic from the export (permalink stub, optional -c category) and then attach comments. It now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote, which GETs t[:link] and returns nothing usable if the historical URL 404s, redirects oddly, or open() raises. The exception is not rescued inside the thread loop, so one dead link aborts the rest of the file (the ensure only restores the email blacklist and rate limiter). The category option and category_id lookup were removed, and TopicEmbed.import has no category argument, so surviving imports also land in the wrong category.

Embed controller specs assert the wrong control flow

The success example expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retrieve` to run inside the request. EmbedController#best does not do that; it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, …)` and renders loading. That expectation fails. The other success example renders best.html.erb, which currently cannot compile (`end if`), so the after-hook `response.should be_success` fails as well. The specs will not catch the enqueue/host/throttle behavior that actually shipped.

Post jobs are enqueued inside the outer import transaction

import wraps PostCreator.create in Topic.transaction. PostCreator commits its own nested transaction by joining that outer one, then enqueue_jobs (process_post, feature_topic_users) runs before Topic.transaction commits. If TopicEmbed.create! then fails (unique embed_url race, null id), the outer transaction rolls the post back but the jobs are already queued and run against a missing row. Even on success they can run before commit. Enqueue only after the outer transaction commits, and rescue RecordNotUnique so a raced import reuses the existing embed instead of erroring.

Throttle key can stick forever if expire is skipped

retrieved_recently? uses SETNX and then a separate EXPIRE of 60 seconds. If the process dies between those calls, the key remains with no TTL and that embed URL is never fetched again for non-staff users (they stay on the loading page). Use a single SET key 1 NX EX 60 so the lock cannot outlive the throttle window.

Unauthenticated embed GETs enqueue unbounded jobs

best only checks that the Referer host equals embeddable_host, then enqueues retrieve_topic for whatever embed_url was passed. Referer is trivial to spoof, embed_url is not checked against embeddable_host or a rate limit in the request, and the Redis throttle lives inside the job and is per URL. An anonymous client can fill the Sidekiq queue with unique URLs; each job still does work (host parse, Redis, sometimes HTTP). Validate the embed URL host before enqueue and throttle enqueues.

embed_url is varchar(255) with a unique index

embed_url is a Rails string column (varchar 255) and is uniquely indexed. Article and tracking URLs routinely exceed 255 characters. Insert then raises on PostgreSQL, TopicEmbed.create! rolls the import back, and that URL can never be embedded. Store embed_url as text (and keep the unique index).

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin writes a 0-based value into 1-based ordinal-group

-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group are 1-based (initial value 1) and reject 0, while the modern order property and -ms-flex-order are 0-based (initial value 0). The new mixin assigns $val to all of them. Autoprefixer-style output must use $val + 1 for the box-ordinal-group properties. order(2) and order(3) in this PR still sort after default items by accident (old default 1 is less than 2 and 3; modern default 0 is less than 2 and 3), but order(1) will not move an item after default siblings in old WebKit/Firefox, and order(0) or a negative order is invalid or ignored in the 2009 syntax. This is the shared helper the header now depends on, so the off-by-one should be fixed before it is reused.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

false_positives.candidate:
Header category bullet loses its 5px alignment offset

.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet previously had margin-top:5px so the category bullet lined up with the docked topic title text. That rule was deleted. The badges change only routes the existing display:inline-flex and align-items:baseline through mixins, so it does not add a replacement offset, and the new line-height:1.5 on the wrapper does not shift the bullet relative to the label. Category bullets in the scrolling header extra-info will sit about 5px too high against the category name.

Panel right-align does not work in the prefixed flex fallback

.panel used to be float:right (and .title float:left). Those floats were removed and replaced with margin-left:auto plus order, while flexbox() emits display:-webkit-box and display:-moz-box before the modern values. The 2009 box model does not treat auto margins as flexible space, so browsers that only understand those prefixed values (Safari 6.1/7, iOS 7, older Android) keep the notifications, search, and login cluster immediately after the logo instead of on the right edge of the header. The prefixes this PR adds are exactly the browsers that will miss the new alignment, and there is no float fallback left.

Small-action button float is ignored in the new flex row

.small-action is now a flex container (the new flexbox() mixin sets display:flex), but its action button is still float:right. Float and clear do not apply to flex items, so the button is laid out in source order immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the right edge. Short rows such as closed, pinned, or autoclosed actions therefore show the delete/expand control beside the text rather than pinned to the far side, in every browser that honors the new display. The same change also drops the description's 4em left padding that previously cleared the floated avatar, so non-flex fallbacks will overlap the icon and the text. Put margin-left:auto on the button (and drop the float) to restore the right alignment; .topic-avatar's float:left is likewise ignored and should not be relied on.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is never invoked

ActiveModel::Serializer only calls inclusion hooks named include_<attr>?, and every other hook in this file follows that form. include_website_name has no question mark, so it is dead code and website_name is always emitted, including null when the user has no website. Rename it to include_website_name?. As written it only checks website.present?, so renaming alone does not apply the TL0 restriction.

false_positives.candidate:
Same-domain check misclassifies hosts

The non-equal branches do not test whether the website is actually on the instance domain, so the profile label either appends a path for an unrelated site or drops it for the same site. The elsif treats hosts as the same domain when they have the same label count greater than 2 and share every label except the first, which matches community.co.uk with paypal.co.uk and foo.github.io with bar.github.io and then appends the path. The else branch uses discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host), which is true for any suffix, so a website host of com or co.uk matches every forum on that suffix. The common www case fails the other way: a forum on example.com and a website of http://www.example.com/docs has a different label count and example.com does not end with .www.example.com, so only the host is shown. Comparison is also case-sensitive against Discourse.current_hostname while URI#host is lowercased, so a mixed-case hostname misses the exact-match branch. The new specs only cover example.com vs discourse.org, an exact match, and a parent forums.example.com, so they do not catch this. Compare normalized registrable domains (and an optional www label) instead of stripping one label or using a raw suffix check.

website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous field hiding

website_name is derived from website but is not covered by untrusted_attributes, and website_name never calls scope.restrict_user_fields?. For a TL0 user seen anonymously, include_website? is forced false so website is omitted, yet website_name is still serialized. The profile template renders the globe label from model.website_name, so anonymous viewers get the host and, when the heuristic matches, the path of a field this serializer intentionally hides to limit new-user spam. Add website_name to untrusted_attributes (or apply the same guard in include_website_name?) and extend the existing TL0 anonymous serializer example; the new specs only cover a normal user.

true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
totalPages is one too high when the count divides the page size

totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (50 members, limit 50) that is 2, not 1. showingLast compares currentPage to that value, so the next guard does not fire on the real last page. next then sets offset to min(offset + limit, user_count), which equals user_count and loads an empty page. The same formula also leaves the admin on a blank last page after removing the final member of a page, because findMembers keeps the server's unclamped offset.

true_positives.golden_comment: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Add/remove members read group_id but the route only sets id

add_members and remove_member load the group with params.require(:group_id). The new routes are member routes (PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members), so Rails sets params[:id], not params[:group_id]. The client calls /admin/groups/<id>/members.json and only puts usernames or user_id in the body. require(:group_id) therefore raises ParameterMissing and every add or remove returns 400. destroy and update in this same controller correctly use params[:id]. The controller specs pass group_id straight into the action and never go through the router, so they stay green.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

false_positives.candidate:
Add/remove membership failures are silent and the add field is not cleared

addMembers posts usernames and on success reloads the current offset, but it never clears usernames (the TODO on the line above). The selector still holds the same names, so another click resubmits them. Neither addMembers nor removeMember handles a rejected promise. A 400, 422, or 500 leaves the list unchanged and shows no alert, which looks the same as a successful add of a user who sorts onto a different page because the reload does not reset offset to 0.

Creating a group ignores alias_level

create only assigns name and visible. The admin form shows the alias-level combo before the group has an id, and Group#asJSON sends alias_level on POST /admin/groups. update applies params[:alias_level], but create never reads it, so a non-default level (for example everyone/99) is not saved. The client keeps the unsaved value until the group is reloaded, so the admin thinks the setting stuck.

Public members page only loads 50 users and cannot page

setupController now calls model.findMembers(), which always requests /groups/:name/members.json with the Group model's default limit of 50 and offset 0. The public members template only iterates that one page and has no next/previous or load-more control; paging was added only on the admin group screen. Non-automatic groups previously returned every member, and automatic groups returned up to 200. A group with more than 50 members now hides the rest with no way to reach them.

Remove link is shown for automatic groups

The remove control is wrapped in {{#unless automatic}} inside the group-member itemView. With {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}, Ember sets that view's context to the item view (so {{member}} works) or to the user, not to the admin group. automatic is not the group's automatic flag there; it is missing, so the unless is always true. Automatic groups still show a remove button. The server answers 422, and removeMember has no failure handler, so the admin confirms and the member stays with no error.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locale files are never loaded from I18n.translate

translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb only calls load_locale for config.locale (line 68), then either returns translate_no_cache immediately when arguments are present (line 69) or caches that call (line 74). The new FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded! is invoked only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Mailers, Sidekiq jobs, rails runner, and any I18n.with_locale / I18n.locale= path never hit that filter, so the lazy loader never reads the site-default or :en YAML. I18n::Backend::Fallbacks then searches empty catalogs and I18n.t becomes "translation missing: ..." for keys that exist only in a fallback locale — the main server-side case this change is for. Because the LRU cache stores that miss under key+locale+backend object id and nothing invalidates it when catalogs are loaded later, a lookup that runs before set_locale (boot, middleware, an earlier before_filter, or another thread) keeps serving the missing string for the life of the cache entry even on later web requests that do call ensure_loaded!.

No coverage for fallback order or non-request loading

The new fallback chain in config/initializers/i18n.rb (locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en) and the lazy-load hook are untested. Nothing asserts that a key missing from the user locale is served from the site locale and then :en, that pluralization still runs on the fallback locale, or that I18n.t falls back when locale is set outside ApplicationController (the mailer/job path). Without that, the broken load/cache behavior above can ship unnoticed, and a later change to FallbackLocaleList or translate_accelerator can drop fallbacks in production only.

Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain

The accelerator cache key is only "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}" (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72). Resolved strings now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale via FallbackLocaleList#[] and on which fallback catalogs were loaded. default_locale is a runtime admin setting and is not part of the key, and neither ensure_loaded! nor a default-locale change calls I18n.reload! (the only path that nils @cache). After an admin changes the site locale, arg-less I18n.t calls keep returning the previously cached fallback translation until that LRU slot is evicted or the process restarts, so users keep seeing the old language for missing keys.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Passkey form data is only set up when a user is already known

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, and both authenticate() (around the fillContextForm call) and the error challenge() use that predicate as the only gate for webauthnAuth.fillContextForm. Previously the WebAuthn challenge, rpId, conditional-UI flag, and AUTH_CHALLENGE_NOTE were written when the user was not yet selected, which is the normal passkey/conditional-UI login. true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative cursor offsets raise ValueError

When enable_advanced_features is true (the audit log endpoint always passes True), OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with the raw negative cursor offset. Django's QuerySet rejects negative slice start or stop with ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported") before any SQL runs, so this branch never returns rows. Cursor.from_string accepts a negative offset, so a client that sends optimized_pagination=true and a cursor such as 0:-1:0 forces an HTTP 500. The comment that the ORM handles negative bounds, and that this reaches rows outside normal pagination limits, is false: the request errors, and the later trim check len(results) == offset + limit + extra would also be wrong for a negative offset if slicing were forced. The same false assumption was copied into BasePaginator.get_result, which now forwards a negative offset into queryset slicing for every is_prev cursor on all BasePaginator endpoints.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Optimized paginator crashes on datetime audit logs

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to the order-by attribute, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor number. OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses this class with order_by="-datetime" whenever optimized_pagination=true and the caller is a superuser or has global access. Audit log rows are ordered by a datetime, not a number. On a non-empty first page, build_cursor calls get_item_key and raises TypeError because math.floor cannot accept a datetime. On any request that includes a cursor, build_queryset compares the timestamp column to that raw integer (DateTimePaginator converts via fromtimestamp and a multiplier; this class does not), which PostgreSQL rejects. The opt-in path therefore returns HTTP 500 for every organization that has audit log entries instead of a page of results.
