Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.

false_positives.candidate:
Same-integration guard skips every linked issue, not just the one that webhooked

should_sync returns False whenever sync_source.integration_id matches the installation's integration, before looking at which external issue is being updated. sync_group_assignee_outbound enqueues one task per GroupLink and each task applies that same check. A group linked to two issues on one Jira (or other) integration will therefore not push the new assignee to the sibling ticket after an inbound change. Previously every linked external issue was updated. AssignmentSource only stores source_name, integration_id, and queued, so the worker cannot skip write-back only for the issue key that fired the webhook. Sibling tickets keep a stale assignee until someone assigns the Sentry issue directly. A write to a different issue on that integration would not by itself loop if the mapped Sentry user is unchanged, because GroupAssignee.assign does not emit outbound sync when the user id does not change.

Tests never prove other integrations still sync, or that inbound wiring suppresses the echo

The new test only assigns with AssignmentSource.from_integration on the same single integration and asserts sync_assignee_outbound was not called. A regression that skips outbound sync whenever any assignment_source is set would still pass, and so would removing assignment_source= from sync_group_assignee_inbound. Nothing covers a second linked integration still receiving the outbound call, deassign with a matching source, or from_dict(to_dict()) preserving integration_id and a real datetime. true_positives.golden_comment: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.

Registered metric-alert handler is now uninstantiable

MetricAlertDetectorHandler is still the detector_handler for the registered MetricAlertFire group type, but it now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and implements none of the abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data). Detector.detector_handler constructs the class on access, and process_detectors does not catch that error, so a single metric_alert_fire detector aborts processing for the whole batch. evaluate docstring still says it returns a list

Callers following the docstring will iterate the dict keys (group keys) instead of the result values.

true_positives.golden_comment: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Occurrence helper ignores value, and several expectations pass the wrong one

build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts value but never puts it on the IssueOccurrence or event_data, so equality cannot tell whether evaluate forwarded the measured value into build_occurrence_and_event_data. Call sites also pass a value that does not match the packet: test_state_results_multi_group feeds group_2=10 but builds the expected occurrence with 6 (line 191); test_results_on_change evaluates 100 but expects an occurrence built with 6 (line 490); test_dedupe evaluates 8 but expects 6 (line 510). A regression that dropped or swapped the value argument would still pass.

false_positives.candidate:
Group-key evaluation test builds the expected occurrence for the wrong key

TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence with group_key "val1" (and value 6) but calls evaluate_group_key_value with group_key "group_key" and value 10. build_fingerprint includes the group key, and IssueOccurrence equality includes fingerprint, so the expected DetectorEvaluationResult cannot equal the value under test. This test fails and does not lock the new occurrence hook.

Occurrence hook cannot see the packet that fired

build_occurrence_and_event_data is the new extension point for emitting an issue, but it only receives group_key, the numeric value, and the new priority. The DataPacket being evaluated is not passed through, nor is the previous DetectorStateData. A detector-specific occurrence (for example a metric alert) needs subscription id, timestamps, and other evidence that exist only on that packet. Implementers must stash the packet on the handler during get_dedupe_value or get_group_key_values, which is implicit and will force a breaking signature change as soon as a real subclass is written. Pass the packet into the hook.

true_positives.golden_comment: The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Issue context sends raw monitor config, dropping schedule display name

get_monitor_environment_context copies the monitor config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with get_schedule_type_display() so the occurrence payload has a readable schedule. The dict it returns ignores that copy and puts monitor_environment.monitor.config in the "config" field instead. Issue occurrences therefore still carry the raw schedule type (the integer choice), and the display conversion never reaches Kafka. Consumers of the monitor context will show the wrong schedule type.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The code fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID when the required data already exists in previous_checkins. This creates an unnecessary database query.

false_positives.candidate:
Failure threshold can open an incident before N consecutive failures

try_incident_threshold treats a monitor as breached once the most recent check-ins (at most failure_issue_threshold of them) contain no CheckInStatus.OK row. It never requires that window to actually contain failure_issue_threshold check-ins, and every non-OK status, including in-progress, counts as part of the streak. With failure_issue_threshold greater than 1, the first failure on a new monitor, a short history after old check-ins are gone, or a window that still includes in-progress rows will mark the environment ERROR, create a MonitorIncident, and emit issue occurrences. The monitor is then stuck failed even though the configured consecutive-failure count was never reached.

true_positives.golden_comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Flusher timers use mismatched, high-cardinality shard tags

spans.buffer.flusher.produce is tagged with key "shard" while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce on the next block is tagged with key "shards", so the two timings cannot be joined in dashboards. The value is a comma-separated list of every shard on that process, not one shard. The process-spans CLI defaults --flusher-processes to 1, which puts the entire partition assignment in a single tag. Each rebalance yields a new tag value (unbounded cardinality) and the string can exceed statsd tag-length limits, dropping the timings this change needs in order to tell whether the flusher is keeping up. The unhealthy counter already emits one bounded tag per shard and should be the pattern here.

true_positives.golden_comment: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Drift wait in test_basic is patched into a no-op

test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op so the flusher thread does not pause, then calls time.sleep(0.1) to let that thread observe current_drift before join(). The test looks up time.sleep at call time, so it hits the patch and does not wait. join() then sets stopped immediately. The flusher can leave its loop before flush_segments runs with the advanced drift, so the assertion on the produced segment is racy. The new poll/sleep was added to close that race and does not. Nothing in the new test_flusher_processes_limit covers actual multi-process flushing, restart, or shutdown either, so the kill/terminate and overlap bugs above are untested.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Spawn flusher workers are never killed or terminated

Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, so they are SpawnProcess instances. SpawnProcess subclasses multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess, not multiprocessing.Process (the default-context class). Both the hang-restart path (process.kill() around line 254) and join() (process.terminate() around line 346) are guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which is always false for these workers, so the signal is never sent. Crash recovery still works because a dead process is simply replaced, but a hang does not: a second worker is started for the same shards, and once it updates the shared healthy_since value the slot looks healthy, so MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS never fires and the original worker is leaked. That leaked worker can keep calling flush_segments/produce on the same Redis shards as the replacement, duplicating buffered-segments output and racing flush state. On shutdown, a worker blocked in Redis or Kafka produce is also never force-stopped after stopped is set, so it can still produce after those shards have been reassigned.

true_positives.golden_comment: Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
