The login UI happens to send an empty totpCode, but the public credentials endpoint does not. Password verification must run for CAL users on this path, and a dummy totpCode must not select the backup-code branch.

Backup codes are lost if the dialog is dismissed

After TOTP enable succeeds, the only copy of the plaintext backup codes lives in this modal, and onEnable() runs only from the Close button. The Dialog is still wired to the parent's onOpenChange, so Escape, overlay click, or the dialog close control hides it without onEnable() and without any warning that the codes cannot be shown again. There is no later API to reveal or regenerate codes while 2FA stays on, and a refresh on this step drops them too. The settings switch can also stay off because the parent is never told enable finished, so the user is left with 2FA on server-side, no saved codes, and a UI that still looks disabled. This step should block dismiss until the user explicitly finishes, and that path must call onEnable().

Download control submits the enable form

The backup-code footer is inside the Form whose submit handler is handleEnable. Copy and Close call preventDefault because a click otherwise submits that form; the Download control does not, and its Button has no type="button". It is also wrapped in an anchor. Activating Download therefore posts the TOTP enable request again (which can error once 2FA is already on, or replace the page) and can cancel the file download, so the main way to save codes fails. Set type="button" and preventDefault, or render a non-submitting link.

Lost access button submits the disable form

The new Lost access / Go back button sits inside the disable Form and does not set type="button" or preventDefault. The enable modal in this same change had to preventDefault on footer buttons for that reason. Clicking Lost access therefore submits handleDisable with an empty code at the same time as it toggles the backup-code field, so the user gets an incorrect-code or second-factor error instead of a clean switch to the backup-code input. Stop the click from submitting.

Missing-backup-codes copy points at a screen that does not exist

missing_backup_codes says "Please generate them in your settings." Nothing in this PR adds a settings action to generate or rotate backup codes after 2FA is already on; setup refuses when twoFactorEnabled is true, and existing users who enabled 2FA before the migration have a null backupCodes column. Shown at login or when disabling 2FA, the message tells a locked-out user to do something they cannot do. The string should say that codes are only issued during 2FA setup and that an account with none cannot use this fallback.

No test covers backup-code login or single use

The new login and disable-with-backup-code paths are untested. The file's own TODO calls out login and disabling 2FA with a backup code, and the checklist says no test proves the feature. The enable test never clicks backup-codes-close or asserts the codes, and the other test only checks the download filename and that a toast appears, not the file contents, clipboard text, a successful backup-code sign-in, or that a used code is rejected. Those gaps would miss the password bypass, case-sensitive compare, and non-atomic consumption bugs.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google update no longer falls back to a destination calendar id

updateEvent sets calendarId to externalCalendarId, or else find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId). When externalCalendarId is null or empty that comparison cannot match, so calendarId is undefined and events.update is called with no calendar id. The old code used destinationCalendar.externalId. Bookings whose references have no externalCalendarId (older rows, or creates that did not persist one) can no longer be rescheduled or updated on Google. deleteEvent has the same dead find, but still falls back to "primary"; update does not.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point at the same logic error. The fallback find compares cal.externalId to externalCalendarId, which is the same value that was just checked, so the lookup can never produce a useful result. The candidate goes further and explains the consequence: the calendar id ends up undefined. It is the same underlying bug.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

Organization slug is stored under the opposite billing flag

The spread was changed from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug } to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}. That inverts org creation: self-hosted (billing disabled) organizations are created with no slug, so org URLs do not resolve, and billing-enabled organizations get slug set immediately instead of only requestedSlug pending approval. The requestedSlug line below was only rewritten from && to a ternary and is unchanged in meaning. This is unrelated to destination calendars and breaks org provisioning.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: the slug condition was flipped to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED. As a result, both slug and requestedSlug get set when billing is enabled, and neither is set when billing is disabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Non-Google adapters still write only the first destination calendar

CalendarManager now passes credential.id into createEvent so each host credential can target its own calendar, but Office 365 createEvent ignores that argument and always posts to destinationCalendar[0].externalId (or /me/calendar/events). Lark createEvent/updateEvent/deleteEvent (larkcalendar CalendarService.ts around line 129) and CalDAV createEvent (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts around line 162) do the same and only read index 0. For a second host, the request is made with that host's token against the first host's calendar id. Office/Lark fail the call; CalDAV filters to no calendars and still returns success, so the host silently gets no event. The collective multi-host fix therefore only works for Google.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same thing: Lark and Office365 createEvent ignore or don't accept the new credentialId parameter. The golden comment frames it as a broken interface contract (wrong signature). The candidate frames it as a behavioral bug, where the credential is ignored and the event is written to the wrong calendar. The root cause is the same: these implementations were not updated for credentialId.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One missing calendar credential aborts every calendar update

updateAllCalendarEvents pushes updateEvent(credential, ...) even when credential is still undefined after the DB lookup (no row, or app.slug missing). getCalendar then throws inside the for-loop, before Promise.all and before later references are handled. The catch maps every calendar reference to success: false and no longer logs the error (console.error was removed), so a single bad host credential silently fails reschedule, location change, and attendee updates for every host.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same problem: updateEvent is called with an undefined credential when the credential lookup fails, which causes a runtime error. The candidate adds detail about the consequences, but the underlying issue is identical.

false_positives.candidate:
Google Meet bookings crash when destinationCalendar is missing

The Google Meet fallback now reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration after destructuring evt.destinationCalendar ?? []. If the array is missing or empty (the new call sites pass null or []), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and this throws before any calendar event is created. The previous code used optional chaining (destinationCalendar?.integration), which fell back to Cal Video. Any Meet booking without a destination calendar now fails inside EventManager.create instead of booking.

Video booking references no longer store credentialId

referencesToCreate now sets credentialId only when the result type includes "_calendar", and forces undefined otherwise. Previously non-calendar results kept result.credentialId. Cancel (and any later video cleanup that looks up bookingReference.credentialId) will not find the Zoom/Daily/Meet credential, so the video meeting is left running after the booking is cancelled. New bookings created after this change are affected; updateLocation still copies result.credentialId, so the two paths disagree.

Google organizer email is always the first destination calendar

createEvent (and updateEvent) always uses destinationCalendar[0].externalId as the organizer attendee email, while the calendar written to is chosen by credentialId. EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per host credential with the full array, so host 2's insert is authenticated as host 2 but marked organizer with host 1's calendar id. Google rejects that insert or creates the event under the wrong organizer, so secondary collective hosts do not get a correct event even on Google.

Collective host calendars are dropped when the organizer has none

destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, and the collective branch then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). Optional chaining does not assign, so the array of other hosts' destination calendars is discarded. A collective event whose owner has no destination calendar creates no host calendar events at all, which is the case this PR is meant to fix. Initialize the array before pushing (for example evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]).

Confirm and payment flows still pass a single destination calendar

Only handleNewBooking appends every collective host's destinationCalendar before EventManager.create. confirm.handler, the Stripe webhook (packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts around lines 119 and 229), and the PayPal webhook (paypal-webhook.ts around line 152) still build evt.destinationCalendar from booking.destinationCalendar or the booking owner's calendar only. Collective events that require confirmation or payment create calendar events on that later path, so the other hosts never get a calendar event or a booking reference. Reschedule/cancel then have nothing to update for those hosts.

Cancelling remaining recurring events only deletes the first calendar reference

The new multi-reference loop wraps the recurring allRemainingBookings branch, but that branch still does updatedBookings references.find for a single _calendar reference and deletes it with every calendar credential on the booking owner, not with reference.credentialId. It also runs once per outer reference, so the same first event is deleted repeatedly. Other hosts' calendar events on the recurring series are never deleted, and a credential that does not own that event is used. Non-recurring cancel uses the per-reference credential and is fine; recurring collective cancel is not.

Hangout-link patch uses an undefined calendar id

Insert uses selectedCalendar || "primary", but the follow-up events.patch that writes the Meet link into the description passes calendarId: selectedCalendar with no fallback. selectedCalendar is undefined whenever no destination entry matches credentialId (or externalId is null). The event is created on primary and the patch is sent to an undefined calendar, so the description never gets the hangout link. Previously selectedCalendar was always an external id or "primary".

Webhook destinationCalendar changed from object to array

CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now DestinationCalendar[] | null, and BOOKING_* webhook payloads spread that field. Subscribers that read destinationCalendar.integration, .externalId, or .credentialId will break. The change is labeled a non-breaking bug fix. Payloads are also inconsistent: handleNewBooking still sends null when unset, while confirm/cancel/payment send []. The e2e fixture was only updated for BOOKING_REJECTED (null to []), so BOOKING_CREATED still expects null and does not lock the new array shape.

false_negatives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One app import failure fails every calendar lookup

getCalendar awaits appStore[type] with no try/catch. A rejected dynamic import now rejects the returned promise, whereas the old synchronous registry lookup only returned null for an unimplemented service. getCachedResults does await Promise.all on every calendar credential's getCalendar call, so one bad integration rejects the whole availability fetch and the booking page cannot compute busy times from the other calendars. createEvent and updateEvent likewise await getCalendar outside their create/update catch blocks, so an import failure aborts EventManager instead of recording a failed result for that credential only.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments say the await on the dynamic import in getCalendar has no try/catch, so an import failure is not handled gracefully. The candidate goes further and describes the downstream effects, but the underlying issue is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reschedule cleanup uses async forEach and is not awaited

Making getCalendar async was handled by marking the forEach callback async and awaiting inside it. Array.forEach never waits for async callbacks, and the surrounding try/catch only covers the synchronous call, so getCalendar rejections and deleteEvent/deleteMeeting failures become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. The handler then sends the reschedule email and returns true while calendar deletes and video-meeting deletes are still in flight (or not started). On a serverless runtime that freezes after the response, those external events are often left behind after the booking is already marked CANCELLED.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem. forEach with async callbacks is not awaited, so calendar and video deletions run unawaited, rejections go unhandled because try/catch doesn't cover them, and cleanup may be left incomplete.

false_positives.candidate:
requestReschedule does not wait for integration teardown

requestReschedule now awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach ignores the promises, nothing collects them, and there is no try/catch. The mutation then sends the reschedule email and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks and resolves successfully while calendar.deleteEvent and deleteMeeting may still be running or may never run if the process is frozen after the response. Organizers can be left with a cancelled booking whose external calendar event and video meeting were not removed, and a failed dynamic import surfaces as an unhandled rejection rather than a failed mutation.

Recurring cancel never joins calendar deletions

The all-remaining-bookings branch still uses forEach(async) and now awaits getCalendar before deleteEvent. That callback is not collected or awaited, and it pushes the resolved deleteEvent result onto apiDeletes only after the await. The later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) evaluates concat synchronously, before those callbacks resume, so the snapshot does not include the recurring deletes. The non-recurring branch just below was correctly rewritten to for...of, await getCalendar, and push the delete promise. Recurring cancellations can therefore return after marking bookings CANCELLED without deleting each occurrence from the connected calendars, and getCalendar failures are unhandled rejections.
